subject: how to plot 2 sets on one graph

messages.author: 4c1108aaddb5744d
messages.subject: how to plot 2 sets on one graph
parts:
Hi ggplot users,

I want to ask that how to plot 2 sets of points on one graph? I did some search but it seems not easy.
For example, I have a dataset, with each column representing Date, Humidity,  Wind speed, Temperature, etc.
How to plot such a graph, with x-axis of Date, y-axis contains Humidity and Temperature points? 

Thanks very much for your help.
Lily

messages.author: 2710b717e5dbb066
messages.subject: Re: how to plot 2 sets on one graph
parts:
If you 2 (or more) y values share a meaningful common scale then you
can use the matplot function to create the multiple plots.

If they don't share a common scale then they should not be on the
same plot, it is better to plot them in 2 plots (close together is
fine) aligned vertically. When multiple sets are plotted together
then the eye is drawn to points where lines (or patterns) cross, when
the scales are different then these crossings are a result of
arbitrary choices in scaling rather than anything meaningful from the
data.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: how to plot 2 sets on one graph
parts:
Hi:

If this is a question about putting double y-axis/scales on a ggplot,
then the answer is you can't. There are, however, a number of ways one
can plot multiple variables in a ggplot, so I'd suggest providing a
reproducible example (Google "great reproducible example R" to find
several links if this is unfamiliar to you) and stating clearly what
you've tried and what result you are after.

Having just seen Greg's note, you can melt the data prior to passing
it to ggplot() if you want to plot multiple variables with, as he
aptly put it, a "meaningful common scale". matplot() is a base R plot
function, however. To reiterate, a reproducible example would be
useful.

Dennis
